note: Good_to_great is as clean a match as exists in this corpus and it is entirely in his own words: 'if I look at people around me, I'm definitely fitter than 95%', 'I want to step above', and a target set at Brad Pitt in Fight Club plus a half Ironman and a muscle-up by his fiftieth birthday. Not_deconditioned is emphatic — six training sessions a week including a 10k run, a strict deficit, and the opposite of gym-averse. Income is scored a match on the strength of the rep's own isolating question, which is the only clean affordability datum in the batch: asked directly whether this was a cannot-pay or a not-worth-it, he answered 'Oh, it's 100% not worth that to me. I can get that way cheaper than that.' A former City stockbroker who chose handyman work is not priced out; he has surveyed the market and declined on value. Successful is a miss as the criterion is literally written — a self-employed handyman is not the business owner, physician or equivalent named in the ICP quote — though the prior stockbroking career shows how crudely occupation proxies for capacity here. Neglected_health is the material miss and the one that mattered: health is his single most active project, running since February at six sessions a week on 1,300 calories, and he had already decided to succeed with or without help — 'It's happening regardless.' The stated ICP would have booked this call enthusiastically and it was never closeable at $4,000, because what he lacked was not money, motivation, or a plan, but critique on one movement family. Read alongside Hamdi Hmimy, Paul Bionaz, Kyle Loftus and Andreas Xagoraris, that is five prospects in this batch who satisfy the aspirational criteria and fail on need, none of whom bought the coaching product. The criterion the ICP is missing is not a demographic one; it is whether the programme has anything the prospect cannot already get.
